skill.name: error-logger
skill.description: Guidance for adding structured JSON logs with correlation IDs across services.
skill.summary: Add consistent error logs and correlation IDs for multi-service debugging.
skill.author: BarisSozen

content.value_statement: Distributed failures are hard to trace when logs do not share context. This skill guides structured JSON logs and correlation IDs across services.
actual_capabilities: Defines a structured JSON log shape for error events.
Recommends correlation ID prefixes for common operation types.
Shows how to include correlation IDs in related log entries.
Documents propagation through the X-Correlation-ID HTTP header.
Maps log levels to typical operational events.
limitations: It provides guidance only and does not install a logging library.
It does not validate log schemas or enforce runtime behavior.
Examples are brief and may need adaptation for each stack.
It does not cover storage, retention, alerting, or dashboards.

use_cases.title: Add service error logs
use_cases.description: Create consistent error events with timestamp, level, service, event type, message, and context.

use_cases.title: Trace requests across services
use_cases.description: Apply correlation IDs to related logs and pass them through service calls.

use_cases.title: Review logging conventions
use_cases.description: Check whether logs use clear levels, operation identifiers, and useful error context.

prompt_templates.title: Add basic error logs
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the error-logger skill to add structured error logging to this operation. Include event type, message, and context fields.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner task for a single operation

prompt_templates.title: Create correlation IDs
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the error-logger skill to define correlation ID creation for these operation types. Choose prefixes and show where each ID is stored.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate task for standardizing operation context

prompt_templates.title: Propagate request context
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the error-logger skill to propagate correlation IDs across these service calls. Update logging points so related events can be traced.

prompt_templates.title: Audit logging coverage
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the error-logger skill to review this workflow for missing structured logs, weak event names, and inconsistent correlation ID handling.

output_examples.input: A transaction handler fails without consistent log fields.
output_examples.output: The skill recommends an error event with timestamp, severity, correlation ID, service name, event type, message, and context.

output_examples.input: A request moves from an API service to a worker service.
output_examples.output: The skill suggests starting one operation context and passing its correlation ID through the request header.

output_examples.input: A team wants clearer log level rules.
output_examples.output: The skill separates failures, retries, normal operations, and calculations into ERROR, WARN, INFO, and DEBUG guidance.

best_practices: Create the correlation ID at the start of each operation.
Include the same correlation ID in every related log entry.
Keep event types stable so dashboards and alerts remain reliable.
anti_patterns: Logging free-form messages without structured fields.
Creating a new correlation ID for each step in one operation.
Using DEBUG logs for failures that require operator attention.

faq.question: Does this skill install a logger?
faq.answer: No. It provides logging guidance and examples that you adapt to your application.

faq.question: What log format does it recommend?
faq.answer: It recommends structured JSON with timestamp, level, correlation ID, service, event type, message, and context.

faq.question: How are correlation IDs named?
faq.answer: The skill documents a prefix, timestamp, and random suffix format for operation identifiers.

faq.question: Can it help with distributed tracing?
faq.answer: It can improve traceability by keeping one correlation ID across related service calls.

faq.question: Does it send logs to a remote service?
faq.answer: No. The skill does not define networking, storage, or log shipping behavior.

faq.question: Which tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists compatibility with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
